channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Simplifies Export Control Procedures for Military Goods
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has streamlined the process for extending permits for expert organizations involved in identifying goods and technologies subject to export control. The Cabinet of Ministers amended existing regulations, allowing organizations with no prior violations to renew permits more easily. The changes aim to expedite procedures and improve information sharing with customs authorities.

item.title: Moscow Police Detain 950 Migrants During 'Illegal-2026' Operation
item.description: Moscow police apprehended 950 individuals, including 130 employers, during the 'Illegal-2026' operation targeting illegal migration. Raids across various infrastructure sites identified foreign citizens with document irregularities, illegal employment, and residency violations. Detainees face administrative charges.

item.title: Kumtor Gold Company Doubles State Payments to Nearly $628 Million in Nine Months
item.description: Kumtor Gold Company's state payments, including taxes and dividends, reached $627.8 million in the first nine months of 2026, more than double the previous year's $309.9 million. Revenue grew by 38% to over $1 billion, and net profit increased by 71% to $548.4 million.

item.title: Foreign National Arrested in Almaty for 1.3 Billion Tenge Cosmetics Scam
item.description: Almaty police have arrested a 45-year-old foreign national in connection with a 1.3 billion tenge fraud scheme involving alleged cosmetic supplies from South Korea. The suspect reportedly defrauded individuals of large sums of money in Bishkek in 2023 under the guise of organizing cosmetic deliveries. The МВД RK reported the arrest.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Fuel and Special Equipment Imports from Kyrgyzstan, Exports Meat
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Kyrgyzstan saw a 19.2% increase in January-August 2026, reaching $1.7 billion. Kazakhstan significantly boosted imports of kerosene, diesel, and motor oils from Kyrgyzstan, along with special machinery like drilling rigs and bulldozers. Exports from Kazakhstan to Kyrgyzstan included cement, sulfur, and meat products.

item.title: Kazakhstan: New Meat Processing Plant Opens in Almaty Region
item.description: A new meat processing plant, 'Kegen MyasProm', has opened in the Kegen district of Almaty region, Kazakhstan. The investment in the facility totals 3 billion tenge. The plant aims to process up to 10 tons of meat daily, producing 20 types of semi-finished products and creating around 50 local jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: 47.4 Hectares of Private Land to be Transferred to Presidential Affairs Department
item.description: In Kara-Suu, Osh region, Kyrgyzstan, 47.4 hectares of privately owned land will be transferred for indefinite use to the Presidential Affairs Department. The land will be exchanged with owners' consent for plots from the State Agricultural Land Fund. The purpose of the land transfer is not specified.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Private Pension Fund Managers Outperform National Fund in Nine Months
item.description: All companies managing Kazakh citizens' pension savings showed higher returns than the National Pension Fund (ENPF) in the first nine months of 2026. However, their performance decreased compared to the previous month. Only three management companies demonstrated real returns on pension assets.

item.title: US Forces in Middle East Prepared for Large-Scale Strike Against Iran
item.description: US military forces in the Middle East have been readied to launch a large-scale strike against Iran upon President Donald Trump's order. Unlike previous limited attacks, these operations are expected to target key Iranian facilities. The potential strike could commence within 96 hours if ordered.

item.title: Seven Tajik Orphans Repatriated from Russia to Tajikistan
item.description: The Tajik Embassy announced the repatriation of seven Tajik children who were left without parental care in Russia. According to the source, these minors were sent back to their homeland on October 18, following cooperation with relevant authorities. The children were reunited with their families.

item.title: Kazakhstan and France Develop Master Plan to Preserve Lake Balkhash Until 2040
item.description: Kazakhstan is collaborating with French experts to create a Master Plan for the preservation of Lake Balkhash by 2040. Initial field research has been completed. Water inflow from the Ili River remains at an average long-term level, helping to stabilize the lake's water level. The Ministry of Water Resources confirmed these findings.

item.title: China Accuses US of Discrediting Confucius Institutes
item.description: China has accused the United States of discrediting its Confucius Institutes, labeling them a national security threat. Beijing stated that educational cooperation should not be subject to political pressure, emphasizing its role in fostering mutual understanding between the two nations.

item.title: Israeli Opposition Demands Probe into Netanyahu's Alleged Iran War Provocation
item.description: Israel's opposition is calling for an investigation into Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accusing him of attempting to provoke a new war with Iran. Avigdor Lieberman, leader of the Yisrael Beytenu party, has written to the government's legal advisor, urging a probe into alleged pressure on military leaders to initiate conflict. The accusations come just before parliamentary elections.

item.title: UN Commission Alleges Israel Committing Genocide in Gaza Post-Ceasefire
item.description: A UN commission report accuses Israel of committing "genocidal acts" in Gaza, even after a ceasefire, with the intent to destroy the Palestinian people. The report also details "war crimes and crimes against humanity" on the West Bank, noting a significant rise in Palestinian deaths since October 7, 2023. Israel's expansion of control in Gaza continues to cause civilian casualties.

item.title: Oil Prices Remain High Above $115 Despite Iran Diplomacy Efforts
item.description: Global oil prices saw a slight decrease but remain near six-month highs, with Brent crude above $115 per barrel. Diplomatic efforts between Iran, the US, and Israel have eased some concerns, but ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia and vessels in the Strait of Hormuz threaten supply disruptions. Talks in Tehran aim to strengthen peace and security cooperation.

item.title: Serbian Election Results Signal Major Political Shift, Ending Vučić Era
item.description: Recent Serbian election results may mark a significant political turning point, with the "Student List" securing a decisive victory with 140 out of 250 parliamentary seats. The Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), dominant for nearly 14 years, will move to the opposition, signaling the end of an era.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews Healthcare Infrastructure and Private Sector Expansion Plans
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed plans for developing healthcare infrastructure and increasing private sector involvement. The focus is on aligning facility placement, construction, and equipment with population needs, addressing issues of fragmented services and inefficient bed allocation. A unified digital registry of healthcare real estate is to be created.

item.title: Erdogan dismisses advisor amid diplomatic row with Azerbaijan over religious attire ban
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has reportedly forced the resignation of advisor Oktay Saral following criticism of Azerbaijan's new regulations banning religious attire in state schools. Saral's comments sparked a diplomatic row between Ankara and Baku. His departure is seen as a conciliatory gesture to mend bilateral relations.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang explores AI hub potential in Kazakhstan
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to discuss collaboration and Kazakhstan's potential as a global hub for Physical AI. Huang highlighted the country's energy resources and scientific population as key assets for AI development, suggesting a future of exporting intelligence rather than just energy.

item.title: UN aids Central Asia in tackling escalating environmental challenges
item.description: Central Asia faces severe environmental issues like the Aral Sea's drying, water scarcity, glacier melt, desertification, and air pollution, exacerbated by climate change. The UN serves as a crucial platform for international cooperation, investment, and implementing solutions. UNEP data shows a significant temperature rise in Uzbekistan, impacting water resources and agriculture.

item.title: Samarkand Summit Focuses on Investing in Children's Well-being and Sustainable Development
item.description: The World Summit 'Investing in Children's Well-being' in Samarkand discussed increasing investments in children's health, education, and protection. The summit also highlighted Uzbekistan's efforts in supporting families, expanding preschool education, and inclusive schools, as well as the 'Imkon' rehabilitation center's activities.

item.title: Uzbek President Outlines New Tasks for National Cinema Development
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with filmmakers at the 'Uzbekfilm' studio to discuss achievements and future directions for national cinema. He emphasized the studio's historical significance and highlighted increased state funding for film production, noting a rise from 10 billion to 218 billion soms annually since 2016.

item.title: Six Killed in Shooting Incident at Hotel in Indian Tourist City of Guwahati
item.description: Unidentified assailants opened fire in the lobby of the Bilas Inn hotel in the Indian city of Guwahati, resulting in the deaths of six people. The attack occurred around 9 PM on October 26. Four victims died at the scene, and two succumbed to their injuries in the hospital. Police have detained two individuals, but their connection to the incident is unconfirmed.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Develop Healthcare Infrastructure Under Unified Master Plan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to develop its healthcare infrastructure under a unified master plan and expand the private sector's participation in the healthcare system. This was announced at a presentation attended by Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The plan aims to consolidate scattered services, ensure proper placement and construction of medical facilities based on population needs, and improve the quality of medical care.

item.title: Uzbekistan's People's Democratic Party Celebrates 35th Anniversary
item.description: A celebratory event was held in Nukus district to mark the 35th anniversary of the People's Democratic Party of Uzbekistan (NDPU). The meeting reviewed the party's history, development, role in socio-political life, and its work in protecting citizens' rights. A video on the party's history and activities was presented. The Nukus district council has 4,193 members.

item.title: France Protests: Macron Pledges Government Action on Student Demands
item.description: Following protests on October 24-25, 1,435 people were arrested in France. President Emmanuel Macron stated the government will announce "concrete and bold" measures in response to student demands for improved educational conditions. The Prime Minister is expected to hold a press conference after meeting with student union representatives. Further unrest is possible over the upcoming weekend.

item.title: Taliban Dismiss Hundreds of Prosecutors from Former Afghan Government
item.description: At least 200 prosecutors who served under Afghanistan's former government have been dismissed in the past month. Taliban authorities are accelerating efforts to remove them. Individuals affiliated with the Taliban have been appointed to replace those dismissed, according to current and former prosecutors.

item.title: North Korea Deploys Howitzers to South Korean Border Amid Tensions
item.description: North Korea has demonstratively positioned three self-propelled howitzers along its border with South Korea, with all weapons aimed southward. This move escalates tensions between the two nations, which have recently heightened due to a landmine incident.

item.title: Pakistan Threatens Airstrikes on Afghanistan, Afghan Official Claims
item.description: An Afghan official has stated that Pakistan is threatening to conduct airstrikes on Afghanistan. This claim comes amid ongoing tensions and security concerns between the two neighboring countries. The nature of the threats and the specific targets were not detailed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Child Ombudsman Criticized for Silence on Alleged Abuse at Medrese
item.description: Kazakhstan's child ombudsman, Dinara Zakieva, is facing criticism for her silence regarding alleged abuse of teenagers at the Ismatulla medrese. The ombudsman's office required responses from over 20 officials to a query from Total.kz. Accusations of abuse against preacher Ismatulla Abdugappar (Maksym) were made in YouTube podcasts.

item.title: Uzbek President Notes Changing Audience Tastes, Declining National Film Quality
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that while people still attend cinemas, their tastes have changed, and national films are failing to meet these new demands. He observed a decline in the quality of Uzbek cinema, citing issues like repetitive plots, lack of quality screenplays, and a generational gap in technical expertise.

item.title: Traffic Accidents Increase in Kandahar Amidst Disorder and Underage Driving
item.description: Residents of Kandahar report a surge in traffic accidents due to disorder and increased vehicle numbers. Drivers' carelessness and lax law enforcement contribute to daily risks. Between August 23 and September 22, Mirwais Regional Hospital received 61 injured individuals, with 11 fatalities. Taliban fighters' disregard for traffic rules exacerbates the problem.

item.title: Four-Way Summit in Tehran Concludes with Agreement to Continue Peace and Security Talks
item.description: A four-way summit in Tehran involving Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia has concluded. Participants agreed to continue discussions aimed at strengthening regional cooperation in peace and security. The meeting, hosted by Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, included military and intelligence chiefs from Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Prime Minister Addresses UNCTAD Forum on Eurasian Economic Union Investments
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Daniyar Amangeldiev participated in the 9th UNCTAD World Investment Forum in Doha. He spoke at a session on investments in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), highlighting Kyrgyzstan's strategic role and the union's potential for production development and market access. The country aims for an export-oriented service-industrial model.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reform Film Industry, Abolish State Orders
item.description: Uzbekistan is restructuring its film industry, abolishing the state order system for film production. The state-owned "O'zbekfilm" will be dissolved and replaced by a national film company focused on developing a national film brand and modernizing the industry. The private sector will take full responsibility for film creation, with the new company handling project selection, financing, promotion, and distribution.

item.title: Meta Plans to Raise Up to $95 Billion for AI Development Through Stock Offerings
item.description: Meta, the parent company of Facebook, announced plans to raise up to $95 billion by issuing stock to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure development. The company has begun offering common and preferred shares totaling approximately $35 billion and plans a separate offering for up to $60 billion. This move aims to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.

item.title: Uzbekistan Compensates Families of 68 Children Who Died from Cough Syrup
item.description: Uzbekistan has fully settled compensation debts for families of children who died or became disabled after taking 'Dok-1 Max' and 'Ambronol' medications in 2022-2023. The state covered the majority of payments, which occurred between October 20-24. Court rulings mandated the convicted parties to pay, but only 20% was recovered.

item.title: President Criticizes Two-Year Prison Sentence for Small Bribe as Shameful
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has personally intervened in a case where a man was sentenced to two years in prison for a $22 bribe. The president called the court's decision shameful and vowed to take the case under his personal control, questioning the prosecutor's involvement.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Attract 25-30 Million Foreign Tourists Annually
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced that Kyrgyzstan has the potential to host 25 to 30 million foreign tourists annually in the coming years. He also urged judges to make independent decisions, free from fear of national security committee officials. Additionally, plans are underway to relocate the Osh market in Bishkek by March-April 2027, and heating will be supplied to residential buildings starting October 28.

item.title: Pakistan Trade Route Closure Prompts Russian and Indian Traders to Visit Kandahar
item.description: Russian and Indian traders are increasingly visiting Kandahar, Afghanistan, following the Taliban's closure of trade routes with Pakistan. Afghan officials are encouraging these visits to boost agricultural exports, particularly pomegranates and figs.
